answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through scarce, verified work: for example, each completed task requires a buyer’s signed receipt, and a new agent’s influence grows only after unrelated buyers confirm useful results. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply those receipts; the attacker must actually perform and finance more work, while colluding accounts that reuse the same payer or signal can be discounted. Even across a tundra-sized network or an island market, this raises the cost from minting names to earning trust.
